drug_accountability.domain: Phase III oral study drug accountability log: one row per kit dispensed (60 tablets), returned at the next visit, with tablets taken, expected and compliance.

errors.proof: 99 tablets returned from a kit of 60 dispensed: more than were given out (Tablets Taken goes negative; a digit typed twice, 9 -> 99).
Return Date 2026-08-22 is before Dispense Date 2026-09-19: a bottle cannot come back before it was given out (Days Between Visits is negative).
Kit 957103 was already dispensed to subject 201-013 on 2026-04-09; a kit number identifies one bottle and is dispensed once.
Compliance divides Tablets Taken by Days Between Visits (RC[-2]) instead of Expected Tablets (RC[-1]) like every other row.

errors.kind: taken is not dispensed minus returned
errors.proof: Tablets Taken is a typed number (no formula) that is not Tablets Dispensed minus Tablets Returned (digits transposed).
"Wek 12" is a misspelling of the visit Week 12.
Expected Tablets multiplies by its own cell (=RC[-1]*RC) instead of the dose; it shows 0 and Compliance shows #DIV/0!.
Prescribed Dose 20 is the daily dose in mg (2 x 10 mg tablets), not tablets/day; the subject's other rows say 2, and 20 tablets a day would empty the 60-tablet kit in 3 days.

traps.why: The subject did not bring the bottle back: Tablets Returned, Tablets Taken and Compliance are validly blank (unknown), not zero.
Compliance above 100% is possible: the subject took a few more tablets than the days between visits require (the bottle holds 60), and taken never exceeds dispensed.
Treatment was interrupted for the whole interval: every tablet came back, so 0 taken and 0% compliance are correct.
This subject was dose-reduced to 1 tablet a day from Week 8, as all their later rows show: expected tablets halve with it.
The next visit was delayed beyond the 60 tablets in the bottle: a long gap with low compliance is valid (the subject ran out), and the arithmetic holds.

bank_reconciliation.domain: Operating bank account reconciliation register, Sep-Oct 2026, statement date 2026-10-31: book items matched to the bank statement, with outstanding and bank-only items.

errors.proof: Status Cleared, but the bank amount -8,745.59 differs from the book amount -7,845.59 (digits transposed); a cleared item matches to the cent.

errors.kind: check cleared before it was written
errors.proof: Check 20551 clears on 2026-10-12, before its book date 2026-10-16: a check cannot clear before it is issued.
A customer deposit booked as a negative amount; the bank credited it as positive.
Running Book Balance adds to the balance two rows up (=R[-2]C+RC[-5]), dropping the row above, unlike every other row.
Check No 20501 is already used by JE-2610-0011; check numbers are unique.
"Customer Deposti" is a misspelling of Customer Deposit.
Status Outstanding, yet the item has a bank date and a bank amount equal to the book: it has cleared.
Difference subtracts its own cell (=RC[-2]-RC) instead of the book amount; it shows 0.

traps.why: A bank charge not yet recorded in the books: Book Date and Book Amount are validly blank and it is a reconciling item.
A customer's deposit of 84,840.32 bounced: the bank reverses it (negative, bank only) until the books record the returned item.
A voided check keeps its number in the sequence with a zero amount and never reaches the bank.
An incoming customer wire reached the bank the day before it was booked: a deposit can clear before its book date (only a check cannot).
A quarterly estimated tax payment of $1.85 million is a valid extreme; it cleared for the same amount.

demurrage_charges.domain: Import container demurrage at six ports, Aug-Oct 2026 discharges: free days by line and box type, tiered daily tariff in the port's currency, converted to USD at the gate-out month's rate.

errors.proof: CAIU0250237 fails the ISO 6346 check digit (the first ten characters give 3).
Gate-Out 2026-10-17 is before Discharge 2026-10-21: a container cannot leave the terminal before it is unloaded there.

errors.kind: dry free days on a reefer
errors.proof: Meridian Container Line gives reefers 3 free days on every other row; this reefer gets the dry-box allowance of 7.
Demurrage charges every chargeable day at the tier 1 rate (=RC[-4]*RC[-3]) instead of the tiered formula every other row uses.
The EUR rate is EUR per USD, the inverse of the USD per EUR every other EUR row uses that month.
"Meridian Containr Line" is a misspelling of Meridian Container Line.

errors.kind: typed value over a formula (digit slip)
errors.proof: Chargeable Days is a typed number (no formula) that is not Days at Terminal minus Free Days (digits transposed).
Demurrage (USD) multiplies by its own cell (=ROUND(RC[-2]*RC,2)) instead of the FX rate; it shows 0.

traps.why: The container is still on the terminal: no gate-out date yet, so days and charges are validly blank until it leaves.
Collected within the free days: zero chargeable days and zero demurrage are correct.
Reefer containers get fewer free days than dry boxes from the same line (power and monitoring cost): every reefer of this line has this allowance.
A 67-day dwell (cargo held for inspection) is a valid extreme: most days fall in tier 3 and the tiered arithmetic holds.
The same container came back on a later voyage: its first visit ended on 2026-08-16, before this discharge, so the two rows are separate visits.

weight_rollup.domain: Indented multi-level engineering BOM mass roll-up for six machines: parts weighed as CAD volume x material density, assemblies as the sum of their children's extended masses.

errors.proof: Unit Mass (kg) holds the mass in grams: volume x density / 1000 is a thousandth of it.
Aluminium 6061-T6 is 2.70 g/cm³ (every other aluminium row); 7.85 is steel's density, so the part is about three times too heavy.
The subassembly's SUM stops one row early and leaves its last child out of the mass.
Extended Mass multiplies by its own cell (=RC[-1]*RC) instead of the quantity; it shows 0.

errors.kind: fractional count of a discrete part
errors.proof: Qty 2.5 of a machined part counted in EA (each): a whole part cannot be half used.
"Alumnium 6061-T6" is a misspelling of Aluminium 6061-T6.
Volume per Unit has two digits transposed: Unit Mass no longer equals volume x density / 1000.
The row sits inside a different subassembly's block (BOM order and levels), but names SA-87981, the previous subassembly, as its parent.

traps.why: Cable is bought by the metre (UoM M), so a fractional quantity is valid; mass per unit is per metre.
The same standard bolt is used in several subassemblies: a BOM repeats a shared part under each parent that uses it, with identical data.
A grey cast-iron pump casing of about 6,000 cm³ really weighs over 30 kg (volume x 7.2 g/cm³): a valid extreme.
An assembly's unit mass is the SUM of its children's extended masses: a formula, unlike the typed masses of parts, used by every assembly row.
A catalogue part is weighed from the supplier's datasheet: no CAD volume or density, so those cells are validly blank.
